messages.content: Let's write `config/locales/en.yml`.
messages.thinking:
**My Localization Project Game Plan**

Alright, let's get down to business and craft those crucial `config/locales/en.yml` and `config/locales/ja.yml` files. This demands precision; it's localization, not just translation! Here's how I'm approaching this:

Firstly, YAML syntax is critical. I'm going to be paranoid about it. Specifically, I *must* remember the YAML 1.1 quirks: `on:`, `off:`, `yes:`, and `no:` *have* to be quoted. No implicit booleans or YAML will break. I need to catch those before they bite me.

Secondly, for the `:en` file, I'm aiming for *perfect* fidelity to the original English. Every character has to match. This means paying excruciating attention to those subtle but significant details: curly quotes, em dashes, non-breaking spaces, the whole shebang. The goal is identical rendering, preserving the exact experience.

Thirdly, for `:ja`, it's not a direct transcription. It needs to be natural, complete, idiomatic Japanese throughout. I need to account for everything - all screens, emails, notifications, Playground cards, the entire user interface. Translation must be seamless, making sure all validations, screen reader labels, tooltips, date/time formats, number units, `distance_in_words` calls, and ActiveRecord attributes/models are all fully and correctly translated. It has to *feel* Japanese, not just sound like a literal translation.

Finally, the verification process. After generating both `en.yml` and `ja.yml`, I'm going to run a Ruby script to validate every aspect. I'll need to confirm that both files parse correctly with Psych, ensuring syntax is pristine. I'll also confirm that every single `t("...")` key found in the `app/` and `lib/` directories exists in both YAML files. And, of course, that every key in `en.yml` has a corresponding counterpart in `ja.yml` (and vice versa), with identical interpolation variables in each. That's the only way to be sure it's all rock solid.

There’s a whole lot more you can do in Fizzy. In the video below, 37signals founder and CEO, Jason Fried, will walk you through the basics in just 17 minutes.

passkey: title: "Then, set up a Passkey" description: |

Passkeys let you sign in securely without using passwords or email codes. To set one up, open the Fizzy menu and go to “My Profile > Manage Passkeys”. Using a passkey is optional, but recommended.

invite_link: title: "Now, grab the invite link to invite someone else" description: |

Open the Fizzy menu, select “+ Add people”, then copy the invite link. You can give this link to someone else so they can make a login for themselves in your account.

back_to_home: title: "Then, head back home to check out activity" description: |

Hit “1” or pull down the Fizzy menu and select “Home”.

assigned_to_you: title: "Now, check out all cards assigned to you" description: |

Pull down the Fizzy menu at the top of the screen, and select “Assigned to me” or just hit “2” on your keyboard any time.

open_menu: title: "Then, open the Fizzy menu" description: |

The Fizzy menu is how you get around the app. Click “Fizzy” at the top of the screen or hit the “J” key on your keyboard to pop it open.

assign_to_self: title: "Next, assign this card to yourself" description: |

Click the little head with the + next to it, then pick yourself.

tag_design: title: "Now, tag this card “Design” then move it to YES" description: |

Click the little Tag icon, type “design”, then “Create tag”. Then, move the card to the new “YES” column you created in the previous step.

make_columns: title: "Next, make two more columns" description: |
  1. Make one called "Yes"
  2. Make another called "Working on"

Go back to the Board view, click the little “+” to the right of the DONE column, name the column, pick a color, then do it again.


After that, drag this card to “DONE” or select “DONE” in the sidebar.

move_to_not_now: title: "Second, move this card to NOT NOW" description: |

You can either select “NOT NOW” over in the sidebar, or you can go back out to the board view and drag this card into the “NOT NOW” column on the left side.


rename_card: title: "First, rename this card" description: |
  1. Click the title and you can rename the card, change the description, or add more information to the card.
  2. Then, hit "Mark as Done" at the bottom of the card.
  3. Finally, hit “Back to Playground” in the top left of the screen to go back to the board.
EOF

passkey: title: "次に、パスキーを設定する" description: |

パスキーを使うと、パスワードやメール認証コードを使わずに安全にサインインできます。設定するには、Fizzyメニューを開いて「プロフィール > パスキーを管理」に進んでください。パスキーの使用は任意ですが推奨されます。

invite_link: title: "次に、招待リンクを取得して他の人を招待する" description: |

Fizzyメニューを開き、「+ メンバーを追加」を選択して招待リンクをコピーします。このリンクを共有すると、他の人がアカウントに自分用のログインを作成できます。

back_to_home: title: "次に、ホームに戻ってアクティビティを確認する" description: |

「1」キーを押すか、Fizzyメニューを開いて「ホーム」を選択してください。

assigned_to_you: title: "次に、自分に割り当てられたカードをすべて確認する" description: |

画面上部のFizzyメニューを開いて「自分の担当」を選択するか、いつでもキーボードの「2」キーを押してください。

open_menu: title: "次に、Fizzyメニューを開く" description: |

Fizzyメニューはアプリ内を移動するためのメニューです。画面上部の「Fizzy」をクリックするか、キーボードの「J」キーを押して開いてください。

assign_to_self: title: "次に、このカードを自分に割り当てる" description: |

横にある「+」付きの人のアイコンをクリックし、自分を選択してください。

tag_design: title: "次に、このカードに「Design」タグを付けてYESに移動する" description: |

小さなタグアイコンをクリックして「design」と入力し、「タグを作成」をクリックします。その後、前のステップで作成した新しい「YES」カラムにカードを移動します。

make_columns: title: "次に、あと2つのカラムを作成する" description: |
  1. 「Yes」という名前のカラムを1つ作成
  2. 「Working on」という名前のカラムをもう1つ作成

ボードビューに戻り、「完了」カラムの右側にある小さな「+」をクリックして、カラム名と色を選んで追加し、もう一度同じ手順を繰り返します。


その後、このカードを「完了」にドラッグするか、サイドバーで「完了」を選択してください。

move_to_not_now: title: "2番目に、このカードを「あとで」に移動する" description: |

サイドバーで「あとで」を選択するか、ボードビューに戻って左側の「あとで」カラムにこのカードをドラッグできます。


rename_card: title: "まず、このカードの名前を変更する" description: |
  1. タイトルをクリックすると、カード名の変更、説明の編集、追加情報の記入ができます。
  2. 次に、カード下部にある「完了にする」を押します。
  3. 最後に、画面左上の「Playgroundに戻る」を押してボードに戻ります。
EOF

messages.content: Let's run a script to verify key parity, interpolation variables, and that every `t(...)` key in the codebase exists in both `:en` and `:ja`.
messages.thinking:
Here's my summary, as I see it:

**Validation Script Thoughts**

Okay, time to get serious about this localization validation. I'm going to kick off a script with `bin/rails runner`. The goal is to make absolutely sure our YAML files are rock solid and that our translations are consistent and complete.

First, the basic check: can both the `en.yml` and `ja.yml` files even load without throwing errors? This is the starting point, the foundation.

Next, I need to confirm that we haven't lost anything in translation. I'll meticulously compare the keys in both files. I'm going to be smart about this, though, I'm not going to bother with the standard Rails keys (like `date`, `time`, etc.), I know those are fine. I'm focused on the custom application-specific keys that we've created. I'll make sure every key in `en.yml` has a corresponding key in `ja.yml`, and vice-versa. No orphans allowed!

Finally, and this is the really critical part, I need to trace *every* `t("...")` key that's used in our codebase. I'm talking about *all* the Ruby files and ERB templates in the `app` and `lib` directories. I'll ensure that those keys resolve correctly in both the `:en` and `:ja` contexts. The script will also check if the interpolation variables, those `%{...}` placeholders, match up between English and Japanese. We need those variable placeholders to be consistent, or else we'll end up with hard-to-debug runtime issues.

arguments.command:
bin/rails runner '
  en = YAML.load_file("config/locales/en.yml")["en"]
  ja = YAML.load_file("config/locales/ja.yml")["ja"]

  def flatten_keys(hash, prefix = nil, out = {})
    hash.each do |k, v|
      full = prefix ? "#{prefix}.#{k}" : k.to_s
      if v.is_a?(Hash) && !(%w[ one other zero few many two ].include?(v.keys.first.to_s))
        flatten_keys(v, full, out)
      else
        out[full] = v
      end
    end
    out
  end

  en_flat = flatten_keys(en)
  ja_flat = flatten_keys(ja)

  rails_builtin_prefixes = %w[ date. time. datetime. number. support. helpers. errors. activerecord. activemodel. ]

  missing_in_ja = en_flat.keys.reject { |k| ja_flat.key?(k) }
  puts "Missing in ja.yml (#{missing_in_ja.size}):"
  missing_in_ja.each { |k| puts "  #{k}" }

  extra_in_ja = ja_flat.keys.reject { |k| en_flat.key?(k) || rails_builtin_prefixes.any? { |p| k.start_with?(p) } }
  puts "Extra in ja.yml (#{extra_in_ja.size}):"
  extra_in_ja.each { |k| puts "  #{k}" }

  # Check interpolation variables match
  mismatches = []
  (en_flat.keys & ja_flat.keys).each do |k|
    en_val = en_flat[k]
    ja_val = ja_flat[k]
    next unless en_val.is_a?(String) && ja_val.is_a?(String)
    en_vars = en_val.scan(/%\{(\w+)\}/).flatten.sort.uniq
    ja_vars = ja_val.scan(/%\{(\w+)\}/).flatten.sort.uniq
    mismatches << [k, en_vars, ja_vars] if en_vars != ja_vars
  end

Also, any English text in HTML attributes like `title=`, `placeholder=`, `aria-label=`, `alt=`, `data-turbo-confirm=`, `data-bridge-title=`, `data-validation-message=`, and `data-bubble=`, must be brought to my attention. This script will be my workhorse. Let's make this bulletproof.

arguments.command:
ruby <<'RUBY'
  require "nokogiri"

  Dir.glob("app/views/**/*.erb").sort.each do |file|
    content = File.read(file)
    # Strip ERB tags so we see static text & static attributes
    stripped = content.gsub(/<%#.*?%>/m, "").gsub(/<%=?.*?%>/m, " __ERB__ ")
    doc = Nokogiri::HTML::DocumentFragment.parse(stripped)

    findings = []

    doc.traverse do |node|
      if node.text?
        next if node.parent&.name == "style" || node.parent&.name == "script"
        text = node.text.gsub("__ERB__", "").strip
        if text.match?(/[A-Za-z]{2,}/)
          findings << "TEXT: #{text.inspect}"
        end
      elsif node.element?
        %w[title alt placeholder aria-label aria-description data-turbo-confirm data-bridge-title data-validation-message data-touch-placeholder-placeholder-value data-multi-selection-combobox-no-selection-label-value data-multi-selection-combobox-label-prefix-value data-combobox-default-label-value data-boards-form-self-removal-prompt-message-value].each do |attr|
          val = node[attr]
          next unless val
          cleaned = val.gsub("__ERB__", "").strip
          if cleaned.match?(/[A-Za-z]{2,}/)
            findings << "ATTR #{attr}: #{cleaned.inspect}"
          end
        end
      end
    end

    if findings.any?
      puts "=== #{file} ==="
      findings.each { |f| puts "  #{f}" }
    end
  end
RUBY

messages.thinking:
**My Translation Deep Dive**

Okay, so I'm looking at this `email_change_confirmation.text.erb` template. It's in `identity_mailer`, which is a red flag. That whole mailer was renamed to `UserMailer`, which means this template is likely a legacy artifact. Even though it *shouldn't* be used, I'm thinking, "Just in case it *is* rendered, let's translate it anyway." Better safe than sorry, especially with something this important.

Then I quickly scanned the audit output to be absolutely sure. It looks like it's pretty clean: just a few minor instances of ` `, some harmless JS within `<script>` or `service_worker.js.erb`, and brand-specific terms like "Fizzy", and developer names/emails. So nothing major.

Wait a second...I'm getting ahead of myself. While I'm at it, I need to be *thorough*. Even though I'm fairly certain everything is translated, I need to double-check. I'll make sure to look at  `app/views/user_mailer/email_change_confirmation.html.erb` as well as that `text.erb` to see if there are any lingering English strings hiding inside those Ruby interpolation blocks. I need to run a proper Ruby audit script on all the `<%= ... %>` and `<% ... %>` blocks in *every* view within `app/views/`. Just to be *absolutely* certain. Gotta be meticulous!

arguments.command:
ruby <<'RUBY'
  Dir.glob("app/views/**/*.erb").sort.each do |file|
    content = File.read(file)
    next if file.end_with?("service_worker.js.erb", "_theme_preference.html.erb")
    matches = []
    content.scan(/<%=?-?(.*?)%>/m) do |m|
      code = m[0]
      next if code.strip.start_with?("#")
      # Look for string literals with spaces or words, excluding t("...") and l(...) and data/class/style keys
      code.scan(/"([^"]+)"/) do |str_m|
        s = str_m[0]
        next if code.include?("t(\"#{s}\"")
        next if s.match?(/\A[a-z0-9_\-\/:.#\[\]= ]+\z/) && !s.include?(" ")
        next if s.match?(/\A[A-Z0-9\-\s_:]+\z/) # e.g. DEV, X-Kamal
        next if s.include?("turbo") || s.include?("keydown.") || s.include?("click->") || s.include?("dialog#") || s.include?("form#") || s.include?("filter#") || s.include?("bridge")
        next if s.match?(/\A(btn|card|popup|flex|txt|margin|pad|fill|border|overflow|icon|avatar|settings|events|comments|step|reaction|search|nav|tray|header|blank-slate|divider|list|input)/)
        next if s.match?(/\A%Y|%b/)
        matches << s
      end
    end
    if matches.any?
      puts "=== #{file} ==="
      matches.uniq.each { |s| puts "  #{s.inspect}" }
    end
  end
RUBY

require "test_helper"

class LocaleSwitchingTest < ActionDispatch::IntegrationTest
  test "switching to Japanese with ?locale=ja persists for the session and clean-browser re-login" do
    sign_in_as :david

    get root_path(locale: "ja")
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_equal "ja", identities(:david).reload.locale

    # Subsequent request without query param stays in Japanese
    get root_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_select "a.header__skip-navigation", text: I18n.t("layouts.skip_to_main_content", locale: :ja)

    # Conditional GET with ETag does not serve stale English
    get boards_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"

    # Switching back to English with ?locale=en sticks
    get root_path(locale: "en")
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='en']"
    assert_equal "en", identities(:david).reload.locale

    # Switch to Japanese again, then simulate a completely clean browser session
    get board_path(boards(:writebook), locale: "ja")
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"

    # Clean browser (new integration session with empty cookies)
    clean_session = open_session
    clean_session.default_url_options[:script_name] = integration_session.default_url_options[:script_name]

    # Magic link email sent during clean-browser login is in Japanese
    clean_session.post session_path(script_name: ""), params: { email_address: identities(:david).email_address }
    assert_enqueued_email_with MagicLinkMailer, :sign_in_instructions, args: [ MagicLink.last ]

    perform_enqueued_jobs only: ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob
    mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
    assert_match "Fizzyの認証コード", mail.subject

    clean_session.post session_magic_link_url(script_name: ""), params: { code: MagicLink.last.code }
    assert_response :redirect

    clean_session.get root_url(script_name: integration_session.default_url_options[:script_name])
    assert_equal 200, clean_session.response.status
    assert_match '<html lang="ja">', clean_session.response.body
  end

  test "unsupported locale param does not break the page or change locale" do
    sign_in_as :kevin

    # Default English user stays English
    get root_path(locale: "xx")
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='en']"
    assert_nil identities(:kevin).reload.locale

    # Array or malformed locale param does not break the page
    get "#{root_path}?locale[]=xx"
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='en']"

    # Japanese user stays Japanese on unsupported locale
    get root_path(locale: "ja")
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"

    get root_path(locale: "xx")
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_equal "ja", identities(:kevin).reload.locale
  end

  test "unauthenticated visitor choosing ?locale=ja keeps Japanese across redirect and persists on sign in" do
    get boards_path(locale: "ja")
    assert_redirected_to new_session_path(script_name: nil)

    untenanted do
      follow_redirect!
      assert_response :success
      assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
      assert_select "h1", text: I18n.t("sessions.new.heading", locale: :ja)

      post session_path, params: { email_address: identities(:jz).email_address }
      assert_redirected_to session_magic_link_path

      perform_enqueued_jobs only: ActionMailer::MailDeliveryJob
      mail = ActionMailer::Base.deliveries.last
      assert_match "Fizzyの認証コード", mail.subject

      post session_magic_link_path, params: { code: MagicLink.last.code }
      assert_response :redirect
    end

    assert_equal "ja", identities(:jz).reload.locale
    get root_path
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
  end

  test "people who never chose a locale stay in English regardless of Accept-Language header" do
    sign_in_as :kevin

    get root_path, headers: { "Accept-Language" => "ja,en;q=0.9" }
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='en']"
    assert_select "a.header__skip-navigation", text: "Skip to main content"
  end

  test "public board pages honor ?locale=ja for unauthenticated visitors" do
    boards(:writebook).publish

    get published_board_path(boards(:writebook), locale: "ja")
    assert_response :success
    assert_select "html[lang='ja']"
    assert_select "#not-now[data-column-name='あとで']"
    assert_select "#closed-cards[data-column-name='完了']"
    assert_select "#maybe[data-column-name='検討中']"
  end

  test "fragment caching isolates English and Japanese renderings" do
    original_perform_caching = ActionController::Base.perform_caching
    ActionController::Base.perform_caching = true
    Rails.cache.clear

    sign_in_as :david
    get card_path(cards(:logo))
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Mark as Done"

    get card_path(cards(:logo), locale: "ja")
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "完了にする"
    assert_not_includes response.body, "Mark as Done"

    get card_path(cards(:logo), locale: "en")
    assert_response :success
    assert_includes response.body, "Mark as Done"
  ensure
    ActionController::Base.perform_caching = original_perform_caching
  end

  test "static error pages render in both English and Japanese" do
    %w[ 400.html 404.html 406-unsupported-browser.html 422.html 500.html ].each do |filename|
      html = Rails.root.join("public", filename).read
      assert_match(/Back home/, html, "#{filename} should contain English text")
      assert_match(/ホームに戻る/, html, "#{filename} should contain Japanese text")
    end
  end
end

require "test_helper"

class JapaneseLocalizationTest < ActiveSupport::TestCase
  include ActionMailer::TestHelper

  test "en and ja locale files have matching application keys and interpolations" do
    en = YAML.load_file(Rails.root.join("config/locales/en.yml"))["en"]
    ja = YAML.load_file(Rails.root.join("config/locales/ja.yml"))["ja"]

    en_flat = flatten_locale_hash(en)
    ja_flat = flatten_locale_hash(ja)

    missing_in_ja = en_flat.keys.reject { |k| ja_flat.key?(k) }
    assert_empty missing_in_ja, "Keys missing in ja.yml: #{missing_in_ja.join(', ')}"
  end

  test "all mailers send Japanese emails when recipient identity locale is ja" do
    identities(:david).update!(locale: "ja")
    user = users(:david)

    # MagicLinkMailer
    magic_link = MagicLink.create!(identity: identities(:david))
    email = MagicLinkMailer.sign_in_instructions(magic_link).deliver_now
    assert_equal "Fizzyの認証コード: #{magic_link.code}", email.subject
    assert_match "6文字の認証コード", email.html_part.body.decoded
    assert_match "分有効です", email.text_part.body.decoded

    # UserMailer
    email = UserMailer.email_change_confirmation(email_address: "new@example.com", token: "tok", user: user).deliver_now
    assert_equal "新しいメールアドレスを確認してください", email.subject
    assert_match "メールアドレスの変更を確認する", email.body.decoded

    # ExportMailer
    export = Account::Export.create!(account: Current.account, user: user)
    email = ExportMailer.completed(export).deliver_now
    assert_equal "Fizzyデータのエクスポートをダウンロードできます", email.subject
    assert_match "データをダウンロード", email.html_part.body.decoded

    # ImportMailer
    email = ImportMailer.completed(identities(:david), accounts("37s")).deliver_now
    assert_equal "Fizzyアカウントのインポートが完了しました", email.subject
    assert_match "インポートが完了しました", email.html_part.body.decoded

    import = Account::Import.create!(account: Current.account, identity: identities(:david), status: :failed, failure_reason: :conflict)
    email = ImportMailer.failed(import).deliver_now
    assert_equal "Fizzyアカウントのインポートに失敗しました", email.subject
    assert_match "すでに存在", email.html_part.body.decoded

    # AccountMailer
    accounts("37s").cancel(initiated_by: user)
    email = AccountMailer.cancellation(accounts("37s").cancellation).deliver_now
    assert_equal "Fizzyアカウントが削除されました", email.subject
    assert_match "削除されました", email.html_part.body.decoded
    assert_match "完全に削除されます", email.text_part.body.decoded

    # Notification::BundleMailer
    bundle = user.notification_bundles.create!(starts_at: 2.hours.ago, ends_at: 1.hour.ago)
    notifications(:logo_mentioned_david).update!(updated_at: 90.minutes.ago)
    email = Notification::BundleMailer.notification(bundle).deliver_now
    assert_match "新しい通知", email.subject
    assert_match "以降の通知", email.html_part.body.decoded
    assert_match(/年\d+月\d+日/, email.html_part.body.decoded)
    assert_match "メンションしました", email.html_part.body.decoded
  end

  test "push notification payloads localize in recipient locale" do
    identities(:david).update!(locale: "ja")

    users(:david).with_locale do
      event_payload = notifications(:logo_published_david).payload.to_h
      assert_match "追加しました", event_payload[:body]

      mention_payload = notifications(:logo_mentioned_david).payload.to_h
      assert_match "メンションしました", mention_payload[:title]
    end
  end

  test "Event::Description, SystemCommenter, Filter, TimeWindowParser, and ActiveRecord errors localize in Japanese" do
    I18n.with_locale(:ja) do
      desc = events(:logo_published).description_for(users(:david))
      assert_includes desc.to_plain_text, "追加しました"
      assert_includes desc.to_html, "追加しました"

      assert_equal "今日", TimeWindowParser.human_name_for("today")
      assert_equal "完了", Filter.indexed_by_human_name("closed")
      assert_includes filters(:jz_assignments).summary, "新しい順"

      join_code = Account::JoinCode.new(account: accounts("37s"), usage_limit: Account::JoinCode::USAGE_LIMIT_MAX + 1)
      assert_not join_code.valid?
      assert_includes join_code.errors.full_messages.first, "地球の人口"

      generator = Signup::AccountNameGenerator.new(identity: identities(:david), name: "太郎 田中")
      assert_match(/太郎の/, generator.generate)
    end
  end

  private
    def flatten_locale_hash(hash, prefix = nil, out = {})
      hash.each do |k, v|
        full = prefix ? "#{prefix}.#{k}" : k.to_s
        if v.is_a?(Hash) && !(%w[ one other zero few many two ].include?(v.keys.first.to_s))
          flatten_locale_hash(v, full, out)
        else
          out[full] = v
        end
      end
      out
    end
end

I saw that in `japanese_localization_test.rb`, the `Export`/`Import` tests were creating an `Account::Import` record: `Account::Import.create!(account: Current.account, ..., status: :failed)`. Okay, I've got it. Now I need to implement a fix to this in the two new tests and run them along with the system test.

**Database Schema Debugging**

Alright, let's see what we have here. *Aha!* Looks like `bin/rails db:migrate` did its job and correctly updated `db/schema_sqlite.rb` – good, we definitely want to keep that. However, it seems like `db/cable_schema.rb` was accidentally redumped by `db:migrate`, and this time around the SQLite process has stripped away the MySQL `charset` and `collation` settings.

The solution is clear: I need to restore `db/cable_schema.rb` to its previous state using `git checkout -- db/cable_schema.rb`. This maintains the integrity of the configuration. We will also maintain the updated schema files for both `db/schema.rb` and `db/schema_sqlite.rb`.

Finally, after the restoration, I'll rerun `bin/rails test`. This ensures that our final test run accounts for the restored `db/cable_schema.rb` file, and gives us confidence that the changes didn't break anything.
